title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension with the knitr graphics devices and figure shapes used in practice: very wide collages (100 × 5 inches), and webp, svg and pdf output. Every figure is marked with #| panzoom: true and should open the pan/zoom viewer, except where a case says otherwise.
Cases with an expected opening view say so in their heading’s expect-fit attribute (contain, height or width), which the browser test checks. By default (fit: auto) very wide figures open at screen height from the left end, very tall ones at screen width from the top, and everything else whole.
webp comes from ragg’s agg_webp device: knitr has no built-in webp device, and agg_webp needs units = "in" because knitr passes sizes in inches.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
1. Wide collage, png (100 × 5 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "A 100 × 5 inch collage of 20 panels (png)."
collage()
```




A 100 × 5 inch collage of 20 panels (png).

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:





The same collage as webp.

With only the pdf device, the HTML page has no bitmap to show; this case records what the browser and panzoom do with it.

```{r}

```




pdf only.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
section: 8. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in)
text:
8. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in)
At 192 dpi the collage is 19,200 px wide, beyond webp’s limit of 16,383 px per side; this case records what happens.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 192)
#| fig-cap: "The collage as webp at 192 dpi."
#| error: true
collage()
```




The collage as webp at 192 dpi.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
9. Wide collage with fit: contain
The override: the whole collage, as a strip.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   fit: contain
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "The collage, forced to open whole."
collage()
```




The collage, forced to open whole.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
10. Moderately wide figure (16 × 4 in)
Wide, but readable whole: the size rule leaves it alone.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "A 4:1 figure."
collage(4)
```




A 4:1 figure.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
11. Tall strip (4 × 60 in)

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 60
#| fig-cap: "A tall strip of 15 panels."
set.seed(2)
par(mfrow = c(15, 1), mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))
for (i in 1:15) plot(cumsum(rnorm(100)), type = "l", main = paste("Row", i), xlab = "", ylab = "")
```




A tall strip of 15 panels.

title: E: image formats and very wide figures
text:
12. Gallery of two collages
Left/Right and drags pan along the collage; PageDown, PageUp and the buttons switch collages.

```{r}
#| panzoom:
#|   group: collages
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap:
#|   - "First collage."
#|   - "Second collage."
collage()
collage(25)
```




First collage.

title: Panzoom
text: Panzoom opens figures in a full-screen viewer: scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click or 0 to reset, Esc to close. It works next to Quarto’s built-in lightbox: marked figures get the viewer, every other figure keeps the lightbox. Source and documentation: https://github.com/sekoclancy/panzoom.

title: Panzoom
text:
Chunk output
Mark a code cell with #| panzoom: true. Click the figure to open it, scroll to zoom toward the cursor, drag to pan, double-click to reset, Esc to close.

image(volcano, col = hcl.colors(100, "Viridis"), asp = 1 / 3)

title: Panzoom
text:
Cross-referenced figure
Labeled figures work too (Figure 1). Options under #| panzoom: override the document’s settings for one cell: this figure zooms to 10 instead of the page’s 6, and hides the hint.

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)







Figure 1: Maunga Whau volcano.

Captions and galleries
The viewer shows the figure’s caption. Plots with the same group form a gallery: use the ‹ › buttons, ←/→ or a swipe to step through them. Subfigures of one figure are a gallery automatically.

persp(volcano, theta = 135, phi = 30, col = "green3", shade = 0.5, border = NA)

title: Panzoom
text:
Test pages
The same 12 lightbox situations (galleries, subfigures, captions with math, images in links, margin images, …) rendered three ways:

A: Quarto lightbox reference: Quarto’s built-in lightbox alone.
C: panzoom match: auto: panzoom picks the images itself.
D: explicit marking: images marked with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom.

And one page of its own:

E: formats and wide figures: 100 × 5 inch collages, and webp, svg and pdf output.

title: A: Quarto lightbox reference
text:
NoteAbout this page



This is the reference: the same 12 cases as d-panzoom-selective, rendered with Quarto’s built-in lightbox only. The panzoom filter is not loaded and no image carries a panzoom marker. Every block image gets the lightbox via lightbox: match: auto, with effect: fade, desc-position: right, loop: true and css-class: my-lb set to exercise those options.
Compare each case with the same numbered case in d-panzoom-selective.

title: D: panzoom filter, no document lightbox key (selective mode)
text:
NoteAbout this page



This page tests the panzoom extension. The panzoom filter is on, and the images marked with .panzoom or #| classes: panzoom should open the pan/zoom viewer. The document has no lightbox: key, so Quarto’s lightbox only applies where a case asks for it (the #| lightbox: cell options in cases 6 and 7). Case 6’s first chunk has both on purpose: panzoom should win, and its #| lightbox: options are dropped, so it doesn’t join GLightbox’s gallery. Case 9’s link should still work (images inside links are left alone).
Compare each case with the same numbered case in a-lightbox, which renders the same cases with Quarto’s lightbox alone.
